v2.4.0.evidence_use: anchors the shipped mobile version under repair

v2.8.0.implication: Official shipped-game chronology does not support assuming Particle Emitter or Advanced Filter substrate exists in v2.4; exact v2.4 runtime ABI evidence is still required before execution backports.

SetInputEvent.latest_semantics: register same-floor tagged effects for manual input-trigger execution and write controller input-event state

EmitParticle.latest_semantics: resolve tagged scrParticleDecoration instances and call particleSystem.Emit(count)

historical_nearby_evidence.conflict_resolution: Official shipped-game release chronology outranks third-party compile/reference evidence for exact-version ABI claims.
historical_nearby_evidence.note: The Iridium reference narrows what may have existed in adjacent development/reference assemblies, but the official v2.8 changelog introduces Particle Emitter as a new decoration type. It therefore cannot prove the shipped Android v2.4 particle ABI.

SetParticle.latest_semantics: mutate and tween multiple ParticleSystem modules, play state, locks, simulation speed, and scrub simulation

SetFilterAdvanced.latest_semantics: reflect filter component types, add/reuse components, tween supported fields, track original values, and clean up lifecycle state
required_v240_surfaces: compatible filter component assemblies and fields

TileDimensions.latest_semantics: core floor-state processing writes scrFloor.lengthMult and scrFloor.widthMult rather than requiring a later ffx runtime class
required_v240_surfaces: a proven v2.4 floor-state application point with equivalent propagation semantics

width_length.parser_mapping: JSON keys are converted to PascalCase before matching declared event properties, so Width and Length correspond to width and length on disk.

conflicting_interface.introduction_context: TileDimensions.ts was introduced in a bulk event-interface commit rather than derived as an exact shipped-game runtime ABI or serializer dump.
conflicting_interface.evidence_limit: A TypeScript interface alone does not prove the serialized keys accepted by the shipped game, and therefore cannot outweigh a parser that directly maps disk keys to a declared TileDimensions schema.
conflicting_interface.resolution: Do not transform or execute TileDimensions from serialized fields until authoritative/current schema and unit conversion are independently proven.

serialized_schema_evidence.assessment: width/length currently has the stronger serialization evidence, but the conflict is not treated as fully resolved until an authoritative game serializer/schema or representative shipped chart proves the keys and units.

runtime_evidence.current_documented_behavior: scnGame.ApplyEventsToFloors applies TileDimensions as core floor state by writing lengthMult and widthMult

current_multiplier_usage.proves: lengthMult and widthMult are consumed as dimensionless runtime multipliers relative to base floor dimensions, so the neutral runtime meaning is multiplier-space rather than percentage-space.
current_multiplier_usage.does_not_prove: This does not prove how serialized TileDimensions width/length values are converted into those multipliers, nor the exact v2.4 floor-state propagation/application ordering.

current_real_install_usage_stub.generation_contract: Quartz stubs are generated against a real game install but intentionally contain only members referenced by Quartz itself.
current_real_install_usage_stub.cannot_prove: Absence of lengthMult or widthMult from the usage-limited stub is not evidence that the real game lacks those fields, because unreferenced members are deliberately omitted.

remaining_blockers: prove serialized width/length 100-to-1.0 conversion into runtime multipliers
prove exact v2.4 runtime fields on authoritative source or device
